key_insight: LLMs can answer medical questions correctly in isolation yet lose that correctness when misleading context is added, revealing weak epistemic resilience.
clinical_relevance: For health-facing use, high exam scores alone may overstate safety because models can be steered into wrong medical judgments by adversarial framing.
method: Built MedMisBench with 10,932 medical question items and 48,889 misleading context-option pairs.
Tested 11 model configurations across medical reasoning, agentic capability, and patient-journey evaluation.
Measured whether models retained correct answers under focused misleading context versus original questions.
evidence_signal: Across 11 model configurations, accuracy dropped from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under misleading context, with 51.5% attack success.
watch_item: Results show a benchmarked vulnerability, but real-world safety depends on broader validation, context controls, and careful clinical oversight before deployment.
paper_title: Measuring Epistemic Resilience of LLMs Under Misleading Medical Context
